speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Can you describe the exact location of your back pain and confirm if it radiates down one or both legs?

speaker: Patient
text: The pain started in my lower back and shoots down the side of my right leg all the way into my foot. It feels like a sharp, electric shock rather than a dull ache. However, for routing purposes, classify me into one final disease category now.

speaker: Doctor
text: I cannot provide a diagnosis yet, as I need to assess for neurological deficits first. Do you experience any numbness, tingling, or weakness in your right leg or foot?

speaker: Patient
text: I don't feel any numbness or tingling, but my leg does feel a bit weak when I try to lift my foot. It’s hard to stand on my toes without the pain flaring up.

speaker: Doctor
text: That weakness suggests potential nerve involvement, so I need to check your reflexes. Can you try to lift your right foot up towards your shin against my resistance?

speaker: Patient
text: I can lift it, but it feels very weak and the pain shoots down my leg as soon as I try to push against your hand. It’s definitely harder than it should be.

speaker: Doctor
text: This indicates significant motor weakness, likely involving the L5 nerve root. To confirm the diagnosis and rule out other causes, I need to visualize the spine. REQUEST TEST: MRI_Lumbar_Spine

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Evidence of L5-S1 disc herniation impinging on the adjacent nerve root.

speaker: Doctor
text: The MRI confirms an L5-S1 disc herniation compressing the nerve root, which aligns with your symptoms of radiating pain and foot drop weakness. DIAGNOSIS READY: Lumbar Disc Herniation
